# MCP (Model Context Protocol) 

> Connecting Claude to the tools, data, and services your team already uses.

---

## 1\. What MCP Solves

Every AI assistant eventually needs to reach outside its own context — into a ticketing system, a codebase, a database. Before a shared standard existed, each connection was a custom, one-off integration.

**MCP** is that shared standard: an open protocol that lets Claude talk to external tools and data consistently, so a server built once can be reused across any MCP-compatible client.

### The Three Roles

| Role | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Host** | Claude Code / Claude.ai — manages the client |
| **Client** | MCP Client — connects to the server |
| **Server** | Jira / GitHub / Filesystem / Postgres, etc. |

### ![][image1]

**The flow, step by step:**

```
11. User → Our Server: "What repositories do I have?"
2. Our Server → MCP Client: Needs the tool list to send to Claude
3. MCP Client → MCP Server: ListToolsRequest — asks what tools are available
4. MCP Server → MCP Client: ListToolsResult — returns the tool list
5. Our Server → Claude: Sends Query + Tools (the user's question plus the available tools)
6. Claude → Our Server: ToolUse — Claude decides it needs to call a tool
7. Our Server → MCP Client: "Please run this tool with these args"
8. MCP Client → MCP Server: CallToolRequest
9. MCP Server → GitHub: Makes the actual API request
10. GitHub → MCP Server: Sends back the response
11. MCP Server → MCP Client: CallToolResult
12. MCP Client → Our Server: "Here's the result of running the tool"
13. Our Server → Claude: toolResult — feeds the result back to Claude
14. Claude → Our Server → User: "Your repositories are..." — final answer

```

**The key idea:** there are two round trips — one to *discover* tools (steps 3–5), and one to *execute* a tool (steps 7–12) after Claude decides it needs one. The **MCP Server** never talks to Claude directly — it only talks to the **MCP Client**, which sits between your app and Claude. Your app ("Our Server") is the orchestrator that ties Claude's reasoning to the MCP Client/Server plumbing.

### The Three Primitives Every Server Exposes

| Primitive | What It Is | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Tools** | Actions Claude can call — create a ticket, open a PR, write a file | Model-invoked, defined inputs/outputs |
| **Resources** | Data Claude can read — a document, DB row, file contents | Application-controlled context, not an action |
| **Prompts** | Reusable, pre-written instruction templates the server offers | Consistent starting point for a common task |

---

## 2\. Transports & Configuration

| Transport | Where It Runs | Use It When |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **stdio** | Local process, same machine | Fastest — local tools, filesystem access, anything not needing a network |
| **HTTP** | Remote service | Hosted servers — most SaaS MCP integrations (Jira, GitHub) |
| **SSE** | Remote, streaming | Legacy — being phased out for streamable HTTP; recognize it, don't build on it |

**Best practice:** edit the config file directly rather than relying on a setup wizard — easier to get right the first time, and easier to review in version control.

### Minimal Project-Scoped Config

`.mcp.json` — project scope

```json
{{
  "mcpServers": {
    "filesystem": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "./"]
    }
  }
}

```

---

## 3\. Claude Code MCP Scopes — Quick Reference

| Scope | Stored Where | Visibility | Best For |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **local** (default) | `~/.claude.json`, keyed to project path | Just you, just this project | One-off tokens/servers for a single repo (e.g. a client's DB) |
| **user** | `~/.claude.json`, global section | Just you, every project on this machine | Personal tools always wanted (Gmail, Slack, your GitHub) |
| **project** | `.mcp.json` at repo root | Whole team, via git | Shared team tooling (Sentry, staging DB, Context7) |

---

## 4\. Demos — Setup & Commands

### Demo A — GitHub MCP Server

**Step 1 — Add the server (project scope)**

```
claude mcp add --transport http github https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_GITHUB_PAT" -s project

```

**Step 2 — Verify mcp.json**

Get your PAT: GitHub → Developer Settings → Generate Token

```json
{{
  "mcpServers": {
    "github": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_GITHUB_PAT"
      }
    }
  }
}

```

**Step 3 — Approve the MCP entry**

- Fire command: `Use this mcp.json to configure the GitHub connection`  
- Check file: `.claude > settings.local.json`

**Step 4 — Start calling GitHub tools**

- Open an issue, comment on a PR, or check CI status directly from a conversation.  
- Goal: compare the pattern to Jira — same shape, different server.

**Alternate — User Scope Command**

```shell
claude mcp add --transport http github https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_GITHUB_PAT" -s user
```

Default scope is local if \-s is omitted.

---

### Demo B — Postgres SQL MCP Server

**Step 1 — Add the server (project scope)**

```
claude mcp add --transport stdio db --scope project -- npx -y @bytebase/dbhub --dsn "postgresql://postgres:password@localhost:5432/dbname"

```

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "postgres": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres", "postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/mydb"]
    }
  }
}
```

- Use this mcp.json to configure the connection.

**Step 3 — Start firing commands**

- Query and interact with the database directly from Claude.

## 5\. Advanced Patterns

- **Sampling** — a server can ask the client's model to generate something on its behalf, instead of calling its own model  
- **Notifications** — servers can push updates to the client outside the normal request/response cycle  
- **Channels** — external events (a webhook, a chat message) can trigger a Claude session directly

---

## 6\. Security & Permissions

- Scope credentials to the minimum a server actually needs — don't reuse a broad admin token for convenience  
- Review Tool descriptions before connecting a third-party server — the description is what steers the model's behavior  
- Treat any server you didn't write as untrusted until reviewed, same as any other dependency

---

## 7\. Top 5 Used MCP Servers 

- Github
- PostgresSQL 
- EXa
- Playright 
- context7

---

## 8\. Key Takeaways

- MCP standardizes how Claude reaches external tools and data — one protocol, reusable across servers and clients  
- Every server speaks in three primitives: Tools (actions), Resources (data), Prompts (templates)  
- stdio for local, HTTP for remote, SSE is legacy — read .mcp.json directly rather than trusting a wizard  
- Advanced servers add sampling, notifications, and event-driven channels — but security scoping matters before any of that
